How to fill gaps in a ratoon crop? Three methods | ganna.in
In ratoon sugarcane, gaps above 20% mean a big loss. How to fill gaps with setts, polybag settling and clumps, and the right way to cut stubble.
Filling gaps in ratoon
When should gaps in ratoon be filled?
The sources we saw do not give an exact day. Settling is ready in 35 to 40 days, so raise the nursery before harvest and fill the gaps after harvest, once the stubble is cut.
How many gaps make filling necessary?
According to an SBI study, gaps above 20% cause noticeable loss. Even when gaps are fewer, filling them keeps up the plant count.
How to fill gaps in a ratoon crop? Three methods
Home › Blog › Filling gaps in ratoon
8 November 2026 · Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics Pvt. Ltd.

If gaps in a ratoon crop are above 20%, the yield is badly affected. There are three ways to fill gaps: 1 to 3 bud setts, 35 to 40 day old settling raised in polybags, or moving clumps from crowded spots. Prepare the settling before harvest.
Why do gaps appear in ratoon?

According to an ICAR-SBI, Coimbatore study, the causes of poor sprouting are weather, a weak plant crop, fungal disease and pests. According to an Indian Farming article, labour moving through the field at harvest also causes gaps. In the same SBI study, only about 40% of farmers filled gaps, because the work needs a lot of labour. But if gaps go above 20%, there can be noticeable loss.
First cut the stubble evenly

With a sharp knife, cut the stubble down to soil level. This removes the old buds and encourages new buds to sprout. Take care that the clump does not shift, especially in shallow planting; otherwise the plant count may fall. Only after this, decide where the gaps are.
Three ways to fill gaps
Setts: Place healthy 1, 2 or 3 bud setts directly in the gap.
Polybag settling: Plant ready-grown settling in the gap. Because the plant is already grown, it establishes more easily with this method.
Moving clumps: Take clumps from where the sugarcane is crowded and place them in the gap. Before using clumps from the same field, make sure they have no disease.

In an SBI study of 32 farmers, 46.87% used bud chip settling, 43.75% used polybag settling and 40.63% split clumps. If labour is short, you can start with clumps from crowded spots, and if settling is ready, plant that first.
Preparing polybag settling
Place the bud facing upward in the bag.
Keep the bags in shade.
Buds sprout in about 10 to 12 days.
Settling 35 to 40 days old is used for planting.
Before planting, cut the bag from one side so that the soil does not break.

Working out the timingSettling needs 35 to 40 days. So if you have decided to keep a ratoon, start the nursery about one and a quarter months before harvest, so that settling is ready to plant after harvest.
What did the Lucknow trial find?
In the multi-ratooning trial in the Indian Farming article, the average ratoon yield was:
Stubble cutting + trash mulch + gap filling: 63.4 tonnes / hectare
Stubble cutting + trash mulch, without gap filling: 55.7 tonnes / hectare
Control: 45.0 tonnes / hectare
These are figures from one trial, not a promise. In your field it can be different depending on soil, water and variety.
Water after gap filling

According to the SBI study, ratoon roots are shallow, so the ratoon feels water shortage quickly, especially early on. Newly planted settling also needs moisture, so give irrigation on time after filling gaps.

How much loss if there is delay after cutting sugarcane? | ganna.in
If cut sugarcane does not reach crushing within 24 hours, weight and juice quality fall. Learn about shade, fast transport and the right order of work.
If there is delay after cutting
Within how many hours should cut sugarcane reach the mill?
According to ICAR-SBI, if crushing happens within 24 hours, the loss stays low. If it takes longer, the loss increases.
Does spraying water on cut sugarcane help?
SBI mentions shade and a fine spray of water in hot weather as ways to reduce spoilage. Fast transport is also needed.
How much loss if there is delay after cutting sugarcane?
Home › Blog › If there is delay after cutting

If sugarcane is crushed within 24 hours of cutting, the loss stays low. If the delay is more than 24 hours, moisture is lost, weight falls and juice quality gets worse. So keep cut sugarcane in shade and send it quickly. Even if Brix seems to rise, do not take it as a good sign.
What do the numbers say?

According to ICAR-SBI, Coimbatore, if crushing happens within 24 hours of harvest, the loss stays low. If it takes more than 24 hours, moisture loss causes a noticeable fall in weight. Heat, burning the field before harvest, injury to stalks and microbes increase sugar loss.
Figures from the Akola study
In a study at Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola, sugarcane was tested for up to 48 hours after cutting:
Purity: fell from 93.05% to 90.17%.
CCS (a measure of sugar): fell from 14.78% to 14.47%.
Brix: rose from 22.40 to 22.97.
A rise in Brix is no gainWhen water evaporates from the stalk, the juice becomes thicker and Brix looks higher. But purity is falling. So do not judge cut sugarcane as good by looking at its Brix.

The same study mentions earlier work in India, in which a 7.4 to 17% fall in cane weight was recorded after 96 hours. According to an estimate by the South African Sugarcane Research Institute, under South African conditions purity falls by about 1.25% a day on average. Spoilage is fastest in hot and humid months. The figure for your field can be different depending on weather and variety.
The difference between 12 hours and 24 hours

In the Akola study, CCS at 0 and 12 hours after cutting was noticeably higher than at 24, 36 and 48 hours. The authors concluded that crushing within 24 hours reduces quality loss. SASRI also gives the same advice: sugarcane should go for crushing on the day it is harvested. So harvest only after the mill slip and transport are fixed. If sugarcane cut late in the evening lies in the field overnight, the time gets longer.
What can a farmer do?
Harvest order: Cut only as much sugarcane as will reach the mill or kolhu that day.
Shade: Do not keep cut sugarcane in the sun. In the Akola study, the purity of sugarcane kept in shade stayed better than that of sugarcane kept in the sun.
Water spray: SBI suggests shade and a fine spray of water in hot weather.

Avoid injury: Sugarcane cut into pieces spoils faster than whole stalks. Keep stalks whole and handle them so that loading and unloading cause less damage. Avoid throwing stalks while filling the trolley.
Do not burn the field before harvest: Burnt standing sugarcane, especially on wet soil, can lose sugar faster.
Immature or over-mature sugarcane: Both increase spoilage. Fix the harvest date by measuring.
Ratoon and care
The work in the field does not end even after harvest. If you plan to keep a ratoon, also see Ratoon crop care.

Is the sugarcane mature? Brix test
Is your sugarcane ready for harvest? Check with Brix in the field | ganna.in
Measure the Brix of top and bottom juice with a Hand refractometer to know whether sugarcane is mature or immature. A simple explanation of top/bottom ratio, pol and purity.
Is the sugarcane mature?
Does a Hand refractometer show pol?
No. A refractometer gives only Brix, which is an approximate measure. For pol and purity you need a lab or a small mill test.
If the ratio reaches 1, should I cut right away?
When the ratio comes near 1, it means the sugarcane is close to maturity. Make the final decision after looking at pol, purity and the mill's harvest date.
Is your sugarcane ready for harvest? Check with Brix in the field
Home › Blog › Is the sugarcane mature?

To know whether sugarcane is mature, measure the Brix of juice from the top and bottom parts with a hand refractometer. In immature sugarcane, the top to bottom ratio stays below 1, and as the sugarcane matures it comes near 1. The firm decision is made from lab pol and purity.
The reason: sugarcane matures from the bottom up

The bottom part of sugarcane matures first and the top part last. So looking only at the Brix of bottom juice can make the field seem mature, while the top may still be immature. According to ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore, in immature sugarcane the top/bottom Brix ratio is below 1. As sugarcane matures, this ratio moves near 1.
How to do the test in the field
Tools: A Hand refractometer and a punch to take out juice.
Choose stalks: Take stalks from different parts of the field. Take at least 2 stalks from one clump. Do not take stalks only from the edge of the field.
Take juice: From the top part and bottom part of each stalk, take juice with the punch and note the Brix.
Calculate: Top Brix ÷ bottom Brix = ratio. An example to understand the calculation: if the top is 18 and the bottom is 20, the ratio is 0.9.
Keep a record: Note the field, variety, planting date and Brix. If you measure again after a few days, you will see which way the ratio is moving.
Brix is an estimate, not the final answer

LSU AgCenter also treats Brix as only an approximate measure taken in the field. According to SBI, sugarcane is considered mature when juice pol is above 16 and purity is above 85%. These figures come from a small mill test and a lab, not from a refractometer.
In shortWhen the ratio comes near 1, think about a lab test or a mill survey. Do not fix the harvest date from field Brix alone.
Check early, 4 to 6 weeks before harvest

SBI guidance says to start checking at least 4 to 6 weeks before the expected harvest date. Keep plant and ratoon crops separate. Group fields by variety and month of planting. Then start harvest from the fields with higher Brix. According to SBI, this arrangement gives a more evenly mature crop, and an improvement of 0.2 to 0.5 percent in sugar recovery has been recorded. This figure was recorded at mill level; it is not a promise for every field.
What affects the time of maturity?
Soil fertility and fertiliser
Irrigation
Pests and diseases
Variety and weather

Immature sugarcane causes loss, and so does over-mature sugarcane. SBI advises avoiding both. So decide by measuring, not by looking at the calendar. According to LSU AgCenter, the lower internodes mature first, and as the season moves on, Brix must also be checked in the upper part of the stalk. Comparing the Brix of different fields shows which field to cut first.

Split the sugarcane: do red colour and white patches mean red rot? | ganna.in
How to identify red rot in sugarcane: split the stalk and look for red colour, white patches across it and a sour smell. Do not take setts from such a field.
How to identify red rot
Can a ratoon be kept in a field with red rot?
No, the advice is not to keep a ratoon in a diseased field, because fungus in the stubble can infect the new shoots.
Is all red sugarcane red rot?
No. If the red colour comes with white patches across it and a sour smell, the suspicion is stronger. Get it confirmed by an agriculture officer or agricultural university.
Split the sugarcane: do red colour and white patches mean red rot?
Home › Blog › How to identify red rot

Split a stalk lengthwise and look. If it is red inside with white patches across it and a mild sour smell, it may be red rot. Do not take setts from such a field, do not keep a ratoon, do not let its water go into another field, and show it to an agriculture officer right away.
First job: split a stalk and look
Walk through the field and look for clumps that are turning yellow or drying. Cut 2 to 3 stalks from those clumps and split them lengthwise. Check the waterlogged part first.
Leaves: At first the small top leaves change colour, dry from the tip and edges, and droop. Later the whole top can dry in 4 to 8 days.
Leaf midrib: Small brownish-red spots on the upper and lower sides, then blood-red spots.
Inside the stalk: Red colour, especially in the lower part, with white patches running across it. This is the main sign.
Smell: On splitting, a mild sour, starch-like smell may come.
Late stage: Stalks become hollow in the middle and break at the nodes.

RememberRed rot is not the only reason stalks turn red inside. If the red colour comes with white patches across it and a sour smell, the suspicion is stronger. To confirm, show photos to an agriculture officer or agricultural university.
How does red rot spread?

According to a review by ICAR-SBI scientist R. Viswanathan, infected setts are the main source. Even in a stalk that looks healthy from outside, infection can stay dormant in the node and pass to the next crop. The fungus can also survive in soil, stubble and dry leaves. It spreads through the field by rain, irrigation water, tools and wind. Spread increases in the monsoon, and risk rises where water collects in heavy soil and when the same variety is grown again and again. Water shortage can also weaken the crop further.
What to do now if you suspect it?
Setts: Do not take seed from this field at all. Do not give it to another farmer either.
Ratoon: Do not keep a ratoon in a diseased field.
Water: Make a bund around the field so that its water does not go into another field. Keep drainage good.
Stubble and trash: Clean the field. Ask an agriculture officer how to dispose of the residues.
Crop rotation: Take another crop for at least 2 years, and plough to expose the soil to the sun.
Variety: Find out from an agricultural university which current variety for your area can withstand red rot. Because there are different types of the fungus, a variety's resistance can change.
Can chemicals save the field?

Do not rely on chemicals for red rot in a standing crop. The Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds guide does not consider chemical control economical. The main remedies from scientists are healthy seed, avoiding waterlogging and resistant varieties. For sett treatment and choice of pesticide, ask your local agriculture officer.
Before the next planting
Take setts only from a healthy, checked field. For details, read Sugarcane planting.

Sugarcane in saline or sodic soil: when does Gypsum work? | ganna.in
Saline soil and sodic soil have different remedies. A simple explanation of soil test, Gypsum, drainage and the Navsari Agricultural University study.
Saline and sodic soil
Should Gypsum be given in every saline soil?
No. According to SASRI, saline soil does not need Gypsum; it needs drainage and leaching with good water. Gypsum is mainly for sodic soil.
What to look for in a soil test?
EC, SAR and pH. Also get the irrigation water tested, and ask the lab which EC method it used.
Sugarcane in saline or sodic soil: when does Gypsum work?
Home › Blog › Saline and sodic soil

Get a soil test done before giving Gypsum to sugarcane. Saline soil needs good water and drainage to wash out the salt; Gypsum is not needed. In sodic soil, Gypsum and farmyard manure can help. The two look alike, but the remedies are different, so do not spend on Gypsum without a test.
How to tell the difference?
Saline soil: Sugarcane leaves wilt early, the tips scorch and growth stops. In severe cases the plant dies.
Sodic soil: A crust forms on top, water goes down slowly, roots get less air, and fewer nutrients are taken up.

South African Sugarcane Research Institute (SASRI) definition: saline soil has EC above 400 mS/m (4 dS/m) and SAR below 6. Sodic soil has EC below 400 mS/m, SAR above 6 and pH above 8.5. Depending on the soil type, the critical SAR is taken as 6, 10 or 15.
When reading the reportThe EC above is by the saturation extract method. Ask how EC was measured in your lab report, because if the method changes, the figure changes.
How much effect at what EC?
0 to 200 mS/m: no effect on growth.
200 to 400 mS/m: slight effect.
400 to 600 mS/m: considerable effect.
Above 600 mS/m: very severe effect.
Salinity mostly increases from poor drainage and too much irrigation, because the water table rises and salt comes up. In a drought year the problem can get worse.

According to SASRI, sugarcane tolerates salts better than maize and soyabean, but as salts increase, yield is affected. For this reason it is better to get a test done before new planting, and not only when salts become visible.
What to do in which soil?
Saline soil: Start drainage and wash the salt down with good water. According to SASRI, Gypsum or sulphur is not needed. Washing without drainage will not help.
Sodic soil: Mix Gypsum and well-rotted organic manure into the soil, then wash with water. Keep the dose according to the soil test report and soil advice.
Irrigation water: Also check the EC and SAR of the water, because salts can change between summer and winter.
Soil sampling: Take samples from both good and poor parts at depths of 0-30, 30-60 and 60-90 cm.
Navsari Agricultural University study from South Gujarat
In a Navsari Agricultural University study on clay sodic soil in farmers' fields during 2003 to 2005:
Giving Gypsum + farmyard manure gave 14.1 tonnes / hectare more sugarcane than giving none, and soil pH and ESP fell.
In paired-row planting sugarcane gave 67.6 tonnes / hectare, and in normal planting 61.2 tonnes / hectare.
As sodicity increased, growth, yield, nutrient uptake and juice quality fell.
The CoN 91132 variety withstood sodicity better than the two other varieties tested.
These are results from one study, not a promise. Find out from an agricultural university which current variety suits your soil.

Burn sugarcane trash or keep it in the field? The real story | ganna.in
'Burn the trash and the field is clean': this belief in sugarcane can cost your soil dearly
What harm does burning sugarcane trash after harvest do to the soil? ICAR-IISR figures, how to spread trash between the rows, and the exception for red rot fields.
Burn the trash or keep it?
Does keeping trash on the ratoon row reduce sprouting?
Do not heap it on the row. The TNAU guide says to spread trash between the rows, so that the space for ratoon sprouting stays open.
If we do not burn trash, will pests increase?
In a diseased field, fungus can survive in the trash, so do not keep trash there. In a healthy field, spread trash between the rows, and if pests appear, take an agriculture officer's advice.
Burn sugarcane trash or keep it in the field? The real story
Home › Blog › Burn the trash or keep it?

After cutting sugarcane, spread the leaf trash between the rows instead of burning it. In an ICAR-IISR, Lucknow report, soil organic carbon rose in the field where trash was kept and fell slightly in the burnt field. Trash holds moisture and reduces weeds. Only the trash from a red rot field should be handled differently.
Myth and fact

Seeing trash in the field after harvest, many farmers light a match right away. The field looks clean, and it seems the ratoon will sprout sooner. But experts at ICAR-Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR), Lucknow write that burning trash carries the risk of losing useful nutrients and of pollution.
Figures from the IISR report
Soil organic carbon (SOC), after one plant crop and three ratoons:
Trash burnt: 0.55% to 0.53%.
Trash removed from the field: 0.55% to 0.55%.
Trash kept in the field: 0.55% to 0.68%.

These are figures from one report. The change in your soil can be different. But the direction is clear: if trash goes back into the soil, the soil can benefit. According to an IISR estimate, 100 tonnes of sugarcane gives 10 to 12 tonnes of dry leaves per hectare per year. Burning this much material means losing organic matter available in the field itself.
Why does a ratoon crop need more moisture?

According to an ICAR-SBI, Coimbatore study, ratoon roots are shallow, so the ratoon feels water shortage quickly, especially early on. Trash spread between the rows covers the soil, less moisture is lost and the root zone stays moist. When trash covers the soil, fewer weeds grow, soil structure improves and the rotting trash releases nutrients.
How to spread trash
Place: Spread trash between the rows. Do not heap it on the ratoon row.
Quantity: The TNAU guide says 3 tonnes / hectare, which is about 490 KG / vigha (1.2 tonnes / acre).
Trichoderma: The IISR report records that mulching with Trichoderma increased organic carbon and phosphorus in the soil. If you want to use it, ask your local agriculture officer.
Irrigation: After spreading trash, set the irrigation schedule according to the moisture in the field.

Exception: red rot fieldIf red rot has appeared, do not keep trash from that field as mulch, because the fungus can survive in dry leaves and stubble. See How to identify red rot and take an agriculture officer's advice about the trash.
The labour question

In an SBI study of 32 farmers, 75% of farmers called trash disposal a main difficulty, because it needs labour. In the same study, about 53% of farmers were doing mulching. So this work can be done in the field. If you tell the labourers at harvest to put the trash between the rows, the later work reduces.

Intercrop in winter sugarcane: which to take, which to avoid? | ganna.in
Potato, cabbage, cauliflower or carrot-radish in winter sugarcane? How much the ICAR-IISR trial affected sugarcane, and what rows and spacing to keep.
Winter intercrop
Which is the safest intercrop in winter sugarcane?
In the IISR trial, sugarcane increased with potato, and the fall was small with cabbage, cauliflower, knol-khol and turnip. Start with a small area, keeping in mind your Gujarat soil and variety.
Can an intercrop be taken in narrow rows?
The trial was at 90 cm row spacing. Narrow rows leave less room, so the chance of sugarcane being suppressed is higher; think it over before deciding.
Intercrop in winter sugarcane: which to take, which to avoid?
Home › Blog › Winter intercrop

In winter sugarcane, take only low, less spreading and short-duration intercrops. In an ICAR-IISR, Lucknow trial at 90 cm row spacing, sugarcane production rose with potato. It fell 3.5 to 4.8% with cabbage, cauliflower, knol-khol and turnip. It fell about 10 to 11.5% with carrot and radish.
What is the benefit of an intercrop?

According to a Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana article, taking crops such as wheat, mustard, pulses and potato with winter sugarcane has been recorded to give more profit than sugarcane alone. It also brings money into the farmer's hands during the long sugarcane crop, which helps with later expenses. But not every intercrop suits sugarcane equally.
Which crop had how much effect in the ICAR-IISR trial?
This trial was done in Lucknow, in sugarcane planted in the first fortnight of October at 90 cm row spacing. Compared with sugarcane alone:
Potato (2 rows, 20 cm): Sugarcane rose 8.25%. But potato was given 160 KG N / hectare, and experts believe the leftover nitrogen reached the sugarcane.
Cauliflower and cabbage (2 rows, 45 cm): Sugarcane fell about 3.5 to 4.8%.
Knol-khol and turnip (3 rows, 20 cm): Sugarcane fell about 3.5 to 4.8%.
Carrot (3 rows, 10 cm): Sugarcane fell 9.89%.
Radish (3 rows, 10 cm): Sugarcane fell 11.53%.
Keep in mindThese are figures from one trial, done in the Lucknow climate. In Gujarat the result can be different. If you are doing this for the first time, start with a small part of the field.
Why is the loss higher with carrot and radish?
Experts give the reason that carrot and radish grow tall and their dense spread suppresses young sugarcane. So the rule is simple: the intercrop should be low, less spreading and short-duration.
A special point about potato

The rise in sugarcane in the potato rows may be linked to the fertiliser given to the intercrop. So do not assume that cutting sugarcane fertiliser and taking potato will give the same result. Count the fertiliser for each intercrop in addition to the sugarcane fertiliser.
Check these points before taking an intercrop
Row spacing: It was 90 cm in the trial. Narrow rows leave less room for the intercrop and sugarcane gets suppressed.

Separate fertiliser: Count the intercrop fertiliser separately from the sugarcane fertiliser. In the trial, the intercrop was given one third of the nitrogen and all the P and K at sowing, and the remaining nitrogen after 30 days.
Crop timing: The field should be free when sugarcane needs room to grow, so take a short-duration type. In late planting, the time for an intercrop gets tighter.
Weedicide: A chemical meant for sugarcane can harm the intercrop. For choice of chemical, read the label and ask your local agriculture officer.
Irrigation: Plan irrigation by looking at the needs of both the intercrop and the young sugarcane.
